## Reaching the other layers

Five keys along the bottom edge and right side. Each still types its own
legend when tapped; hold it past **180 ms** and it switches layer instead.

<table>
<thead><tr><th>Hold this</th><th>To reach</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>`  (backtick)</b></td><td>Media</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Home</b></td><td>F-keys</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>End</b></td><td>Mouse</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>,  (comma)</b></td><td>Navigation</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>R-Ctrl</b></td><td>Settings</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Swapping Colemak and QWERTY

Hold **right Ctrl**, then press **A** for Colemak, **R** to swap, or **S**
for QWERTY — the three heavy-bordered keys on the Settings layer. The board
plays that layout's own tune so you know it took, and remembers the choice
across unplugging.

<div class="pagebreak"></div>

## The two letter layers

Only letters live here. Everything else is dotted, because the Function
layer above supplies it — which is why swapping layouts cannot disturb
your modifiers, numbers or layer keys.

## Every dual-role key

Tap is under **180 ms**. Press another key while holding and it commits
to the hold immediately, so fast typing does not produce stray letters.

<div class="sbs"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Tap for</th><th>Hold for</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>Menu</b></td><td>R-Alt</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Enter</b></td><td>Shift</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Del</b></td><td>L-Alt</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>`  (backtick)</b></td><td>MEDIA</td></tr>
</tbody></table><table>
<thead><tr><th>Tap for</th><th>Hold for</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>Home</b></td><td>F-KEYS</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>End</b></td><td>MOUSE</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>,  (comma)</b></td><td>NAV</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>R-Ctrl</b></td><td>SETTINGS</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

## Knowing which mode you are in

Two signals, answering two different questions.

**The underglow says where you are.** At rest it shows the letter layout;
while a layer key is held it shows that layer.

| Underglow | Means |
|---|---|
| **Cyan** | Colemak — at rest |
| **Amber** | QWERTY — at rest |
| Pink | F-keys — while held |
| Violet | Navigation — while held |
| Green | Mouse — while held |
| Red | Media — while held |
| Blue | Settings — while held |

**A sound says something changed.** Swapping letter layout plays that
layout's own short tune, so you know it took effect without looking.

> Layer colouring stands aside if you turn the light off or pick an
> animation, and it keeps whatever brightness you set. It is an indicator,
> not a hijack.

## If something goes wrong

Three ways into the bootloader, most convenient first. The last one works
even if the firmware is completely broken.

1. **Hold right Ctrl, then the top-right key** — that is `BOOTLOADER` on the
   Settings layer.
2. **Hold the top-left key while plugging in.** Built into the keyboard, so
   it works whatever keymap is loaded.
3. **The `reset` pinhole** on the back plate, top right. A paperclip reaches
   it with the case assembled; it depends on no firmware at all.

```
make preonic/rev3_drop:dooroflife_v2:flash     # this layout
make preonic/rev3_drop:dooroflife:flash        # the 2021 layout, unchanged
```
